profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer, TS/SCI, The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
profile.jobTitle: Senior Software Engineer, Unmanned and Autonomous Systems

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, Unmanned and Autonomous Systems
positions.description:
•	Lead the design and implementation of various data acquisition and visualization systems deployed under and on water for the U.S. Navy, comprising Arduinos, Raspberry Pis, and/or PCs, integrating with both rugged industrial and low-cost commercial grade INS/IMU, power, and environmental sensors – spanning I2C, UART, CAN and Ethernet communication protocols as well as C++, Python, and Java code development
•	Modified C++ quadcopter autopilot code and developed offboard companion computer software to allow for: injection of simulated GPS data, bypass of mixers enabling direct control of quadcopter motors via offboard flight software, and ingest of custom video, inertial, and environmental sensor data for NASA – New Frontiers Program: Dragonfly
•	Served as the principal SW/HW system designer and integrator of a “Telemedicine Airway Management System” that aided development of strategies for remotely-assisted intubation necessitated by the COVID-19 pandemic – integrating video conferencing software with medical equipment and consumer electronics products (smart glasses, webcam, ruggedized tablet, laryngoscope, and pulse oximeter)
•	Developed C++ drivers for CBRN sensors for use on Nibbler quadcopters performing autonomous collaborative search, as well as enabled GPS-denied takeoff and 800Hz IMU transmission for use in visual-inertial SLAM algorithms for GPS-denied return-to-launch missions
•	Lead setup of AI/ML workstations and servers in both open and NISPOM Closed Areas, performed Linux System Administrator duties, and configured continuous integration of code to support teams performing development of neural networks for automated target recognition 
•	Proposed and won funding for “Chaos Engineering for Resilient Autonomy,” an Independent Research and Development (IRAD) project under the Sea Control Mission Area

company.name: The Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, R&D
positions.description:
•	Refactored MotionEngine™, Hillcrest’s flagship sensor processing software product, to use a producer-consumer API, providing input into the API design
•	Designed the compositing context awareness module (in vehicle, walking, sleep, etc.)  for MotionEngine™ Wear, porting many subcomponent modules from MATLAB to C++
•	Updated core components and analyzed predictive tracking algorithms to allow for low latency, 1kHz gyro rotation vector output for AR/VR applications
•	Developed a Python command-line interface tool to reformat data downloaded from an in-house sensor qualification system into customizable test vectors for analyzing temperature hysteresis effects on zero-rate offset compensation in IMU gyroscopes
•	Updated and maintained in-house data replay and simulation tools used to debug motion algorithms deployed in embedded devices
•	Ported a factory planar calibration algorithm from an external calibration system into the sensor hub software stack, adapting control flow for user interactive events
•	Maintained Bamboo projects and servers to ensure proper regression of the R&D codebase
•	Led and coordinated adoption of Conda to streamline bring up of new development environments
•	Investigated faceted search and recommender systems, setting up a Docker sandbox pen to allow team members to explore machine learning and natural language processing techniques  
•	Used optical motion capture systems to independently evaluate efficacy of Google Tango and magnetometer arrays for use in robotic SLAM and navigation
•	Outfitted a single family home with sensor stations (microphone, accelerometer, ultrasonic, piezoelectric) to characterize noise profiles of air-conditioning, heating, and refrigeration systems
•	Mentored a summer co-op engineering student, giving technical and public speaking advice

positions.title: Firmware Engineer, Embedded
positions.description:
•	Implemented embedded C drivers for I2C/SPI-based sensors: gyroscopes, accelerometers, and magnetometers, as well as temperature, humidity, pressure, proximity, and ambient light sensors
•	Updated Java-based manufacturing, calibration, and evaluation software toolkits that interfaced with gimbals and thermal chambers to process, qualify, and license IMUs and sensor hubs
•	Implemented test benches for various ARM Cortex-M cores to debug integration of motion processing algorithms with sensor drivers, interrupts, SERCOM peripherals, and RTOSs
•	Designed bootloaders to facilitate in field DFU of sensors hub products
•	Interfaced with manufacturing and end-product clients to resolve bring up and integration issues

positions.title: Graduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
•	Ported a post-Doppler space-time adaptive processing (STAP) program from MATLAB to C
•	Adapted the STAP program to new airborne radar parameters by generating simulated ground target and clutter data
•	Analyzed real-time performance of sequential and parallelized STAP programs on multicore Intel x86 processors and low-power dual-core PowerPC 440 anti-tamper processors
•	Summarized empirical results and conclusions, submitting regular task reports to personnel at Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR)

positions.title: Digital Design Engineer
positions.description:
•	Designed, tested, and verified I2S and AC ’97 digital audio controllers
•	Characterized PS/2 bus to verify proper initialization and message passing behavior of touchpads
•	Narrated and helped direct English-language product tutorial videos
